lead.headline: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO; Nasdaq posts its best day since April 2025
lead.dek: The board voted unanimously 11 days after he resigned over an affair with an alleged Chinese agent; Trump called it the 'correct and proper decision'
body: Nvidia's board voted unanimously Monday to bring Jensen Huang back as president, chief executive and a director 11 days after he resigned, and Wall Street followed: the Nasdaq composite closed up 6.5% and the S&P 500 about 4.7%, the best day for both since April 2025, Euronews reported. Nvidia shares rose about 31.5% from Friday's close.

Huang stepped down after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who was alleged to be a spy; Attorney General Todd Blanche said Nov. 12 that the FBI was investigating reports she had worked for the Chinese government, and Beijing rejected the allegation. Board chair Harvey Jones said directors were satisfied with Huang's "candor and ability to lead" after a series of meetings and had input from senior U.S. government officials; a week earlier the board had said it did not intend to reinstate him.

President Donald Trump called the reversal the "correct and proper decision" and said the board "acted really responsibly"; NBC News reported that Trump, Vice President JD Vance and Blanche worked through the weekend to restore Huang's position. An independent committee is still investigating whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort, a second will oversee trade compliance, and Huang is due before three House committees Dec. 1 for a transcribed interview that will not be public. Colette Kress, the interim chief executive, stays on as chief financial officer.

briefs.headline: Army says Iowa lead azide detonation will go ahead after court lifts stay
briefs.summary: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said late Monday the Army will detonate 68 drums of degraded lead azide, almost 10,000 pounds, at the Middletown plant, hours after the 8th Circuit lifted its Thursday stay. No date was given.

briefs.headline: Judge unseals 160 pages from the search of Rep. Ilhan Omar's home
briefs.summary: Chief Judge James Boasberg released more than 160 pages Monday night, about half redacted, after news outlets sued; the warrant stays sealed. A DOJ filing dates the alleged violations to 1980, before Omar was born.

briefs.headline: Trump orders DOJ to seek death penalty in child murders and expedite executions
briefs.summary: At the Justice Department on Monday, Trump signed a directive telling prosecutors to seek death in murders involving children, rape and trafficking and to expedite executions. Gallup puts support for the penalty at 49%, a low since 1971.

briefs.headline: Rep. Jimmy Gomez to resign after Ethics panel finds misconduct evidence
briefs.summary: The House Ethics Committee found substantial evidence of sexual misconduct toward a staffer; the California Democrat disputes it but steps down next week, the third such resignation this year. More than 3,700 flights were delayed Monday.

briefs.headline: Hungary's Magyar meets Zelenskyy in Zakarpattia in a break with Orban's line
briefs.summary: Peter Magyar was holding talks with Volodymyr Zelenskyy in western Ukraine on Tuesday, his first bilateral visit. He told parliament Monday that Russia is the aggressor and called Viktor Orban's campaign against Ukraine "hate-inciting."

briefs.headline: Hasina says she will return to Bangladesh Dec. 16 despite death sentence
briefs.summary: Her spokesperson said Tuesday she plans to fly home from India on Dec. 16, the anniversary of the 1971 war's end. A court sentenced her to death in absentia over the crackdown in which the UN says up to 1,400 died; Dhaka still seeks extradition.

briefs.headline: Mexico will try 'El Chapo Isidro' at home despite a US extradition request
briefs.summary: Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said Monday that Fausto Isidro Meza Flores faces weapons and methamphetamine charges at home; the U.S. seeks him on six counts. Officials said U.S. drones were authorized before Friday's raid, in which 20 died.

briefs.headline: Iranian courts order the US to pay $290 billion as new sanctions land
briefs.summary: A judiciary official told state television Monday that domestic courts awarded $290 billion against the United States for actions going back decades, with suits also filed against Gulf states. The Treasury issued new Iran sanctions the same day.

briefs.headline: Troopers find three shot dead in a Kearneysville home; no arrests
briefs.summary: State Police and Jefferson County deputies answering a report about 6:25 p.m. Monday found three people dead of gunshot wounds inside a residence on Lisa Lane in Kearneysville; a search for a suspect was continuing early Tuesday.

briefs.headline: ACLU-WV asks Supreme Court to deny AG's bid to dismiss school funding suit
briefs.summary: Representing a Lincoln County sixth-grader, ACLU-WV asked the court in a 19-page response to deny Attorney General JB McCuskey's motion, which says the court lacks authority over legislative leaders; the state wants the case paused until April.

briefs.headline: Lewis and Wirt prosecutors take over the Kanawha ambulance death case
briefs.summary: Judge Dave Hardy named Lewis County Prosecutor Christina Flanagan special prosecutor, with Wirt County's Austin Grimmett assisting, in the manslaughter case against Alyssa Middleton over John Lucas's April 16 death; trial is not expected before 2027.

briefs.headline: Marshall Health Network to run The Greenbrier Clinic from January
briefs.summary: Marshall Health Network will manage The Greenbrier Clinic at White Sulphur Springs from January under a letter of intent reached last week, CEO Scott Raynes said Monday, keeping the executive physicals offered since 1948 and adding specialists.

regional.item: Cabell commissioners approved a letter Monday backing Marshall Health Network's bid to run day-to-day operations at Mildred Mitchell-Bateman Hospital.
The Kanawha school board took back the former Garnet Career Center from an alumni foundation whose plans stalled and which owes a $40,000 water bill.
Wood County commissioners put $22,000 Monday toward a $737,586 snow broom for the regional airport, which has closed in past storms without one.

away.item: North Bennington's school district sat with four others Thursday at the first Act 170 merger study meeting; the group meets again Dec. 17.

hotspots.item: The former Diana school tops Webster County's list for state demolition money as $10M is split among $44M of requests, The Webster Echo said Monday.
Topsail Beach was awarded a $250,000 Division of Coastal Management grant for access work at its Nature Preserve, the town said Nov. 13.

briefs.headline: Prince George's living wage rises to $24 an hour, $5.75 above the minimum
briefs.summary: Living Wage B.C. puts Prince George and Cranbrook at $24 an hour, against $30.50 in Whistler and $28.55 in Metro Vancouver; the provincial minimum is $18.25. Transportation and food drive the northern figure, the group said.

briefs.headline: HandyDART riders get online booking and bus tracking from Thursday
briefs.summary: BC Transit's new system lets handyDART riders book online or in an app from Nov. 26, track buses in real time and change trips without calling dispatch; phone booking stays, and eligibility, hours and service areas do not change.

briefs.headline: Court orders B.C. to revisit 'substantially started' ruling on KSM gold mine
briefs.summary: The B.C. Supreme Court ruled last week the province must reconsider its 2024 finding that Seabridge Gold's KSM project had substantially started and consult the Tsetsaut Skii km Lax Ha Nation; the Nisga'a and Tahltan back the project.

briefs.headline: New Westminster man charged with murder of actor missing since May
briefs.summary: Nathan Ambros Neima, 35, was charged Saturday with second-degree murder in the death of Stewart McLean, 45, an actor last seen May 15 at his Lions Bay home, the Integrated Homicide Investigation Team said Monday.

briefs.headline: Pentagon fact sheet says Canada's 'defense shortfalls speak for themselves'
briefs.summary: A fact sheet released Monday says Canada has yet to make the hard decisions to meet its NATO pledge, days after Pete Hegseth's memo restricting cooperation. Canada spent $63.4 billion in 2025, 2% of GDP for the first time.

briefs.headline: CSIS plans a 'significant' expansion abroad after $6B over ten years
briefs.summary: The agency said a larger overseas footprint will diversify intelligence-sharing after the Carney government's $6 billion over ten years; it acknowledges stations only in Washington, London and Paris and wants a permanent presence in the North.

briefs.headline: Euclid finds the first quasar beyond redshift 8, 630 million years after the Big Bang
briefs.summary: ESA's telescope found J1504+6252 at redshift 8.13 in 18 months of data, and JWST put its black hole at about 360 million solar masses; the result, in Astronomy and Astrophysics, beats Euclid's own record by about 40 million years.

briefs.headline: New deep-sea clam found living inside the throat of a sea urchin
briefs.summary: Vaticinaria gulicola, up to 19 mm long, lives in the esophagus of an urchin 4,000 to 5,000 metres down in the Great Australian Bight, museum researchers from Santa Barbara, Victoria and Kyoto report; DNA traced it to its host.

briefs.headline: GLP-1 weight loss raised mammographic breast density in 62.5% of women
briefs.summary: In a retrospective study of 107 women on the drugs for at least a year, presented at the RSNA meeting, automated density rose a BI-RADS category in 65 of 104 and fell in none; all four biopsies were benign. The authors said patients need not worry.

briefs.headline: Pakistan's first astronaut launches to Tiangong with Shenzhou-24 Wednesday
briefs.summary: Air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, flies with Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi from Jiuquan at 8:18 a.m. Beijing time Wednesday, 7:18 p.m. ET Tuesday, in China's first crewed flight with a foreign astronaut; he spends about a week aboard.

briefs.headline: Guterres asks governments to agree an AI oversight framework within a year
briefs.summary: At the Bridgetown summit in Barbados on Monday, Secretary-General Antonio Guterres asked member states to build "a globally inclusive and principles-based multilateral framework" within a year, backed by independent oversight.

briefs.headline: Hochul to sign five-year New York ban on AI chatbot toys today
briefs.summary: Gov. Kathy Hochul is expected to sign a bill Tuesday barring the manufacture, distribution and sale of toys powered by AI chatbots in New York for five years, effective in February; the state follows California.

briefs.headline: Claude's Riemann proof runs 250,000 unreadable pages; Clay lists it 'active'
briefs.summary: The proof Anthropic researcher Levent Alpoge announced with Claude is about 250,000 pages of model-generated text plus 240 MB of Lean code, which Alpoge himself called unreadable; Clay moved the problem to "active," not solved.

kicker: Nicholas-Webster and Summers-New River carry no regional line today; the Hatsu basho opens Jan. 10 in Tokyo, 47 days out.
